intro: FireRings Intelligence: an explainable model of why MODIS and VIIRS disagree, honest uncertainty with a coverage check, and a forecast that speaks only where it has proven skill. Every number below comes from tested code in src/compute/ml.
demo_computed: Demo: these ML results were computed by the real models, but on synthetic demo inputs.
demo_mock: Demo: illustrative ML results generated in your browser. Run `npm run ml` for computed ones.

card.title: Model card
card.use1: One continuous monthly fire-activity record across MODIS and VIIRS, with honest 90% ranges.
card.use2: Explaining where and why MODIS and VIIRS counts differ.
card.use3: Seasonal planning: next months as below, near or above normal, only where past forecasts beat climatology.
card.not1: Life-safety or evacuation decisions without local verification.
card.not2: Finding individual fires: use NASA FIRMS near-real-time alerts.
card.not3: Burned area, emissions or damage estimates.
card.not4: New regions or periods without re-validation.
card.data_in: NASA FIRMS MODIS C6.1 (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS 375 m on a 5.5 km grid; MCD12Q1 land cover; MODIS/VIIRS NDVI; NASA POWER weather.
card.data_demo: This build uses synthetic demo inputs: the numbers show how the method behaves, not what happened.
card.l1: Clouds, smoke and short fires between overpasses hide fires from both sensors.
card.l2: Before July 2002 only Terra flew; a Terra-only model covers those months with wider ranges.
card.l3: Area ranges come from a small calibration sample and are approximate.
card.l4: Forecast skill is modest and varies by area and month; months without skill show no probabilities.
card.l5: New sensors (NOAA-21 and later) need their own calibration as they join.
card.safety: Not for life-safety decisions without local verification.
